title: Speeding up the Local C++ Development Cycle with Header Substitution
problem: C++ header inclusion significantly increases compilation time, but forward declarations have complex, non-obvious rules. Forward declaring methods and lambda-taking functions is impossible, limiting optimization opportunities.
motivation: C++ compilation time is critical bottleneck in development cycles, especially in large codebases. Reducing build time directly improves developer productivity across embedded and high-performance computing domains.
method: The tool automatically scans your code to identify places where you can replace header includes with forward declarations—instead of loading entire header files at compile time, forward declarations just tell the compiler what it needs to know. It uses LLVM, the compiler infrastructure, along with a specialized tool called Yalla to perform these transformations. For situations where normal forward declarations don't work—specifically class methods and functions that take lambda functions as parameters—the tool instead generates wrapper functions, simpler interfaces that achieve the same goal. The system uses profitability analysis to determine which transformations will meaningfully improve compilation speed, preventing unnecessary changes.
key_novelty: It automatically transforms header includes into forward declarations, handling even the previously impossible cases—methods and lambda-parameter functions—with wrapper functions.
contributions: Function wrapper technique for methods and lambda-parameter functions
Up to 24.5× speedup in C++ file compilation
limitations: Applicability to template-heavy modern C++ code not discussed; limitations of wrapper approach not detailed.
primary_theme: Automated header substitution for faster C++ builds
